officialTitle: Ribociclib plus Endocrine Therapy in Early Breast Cancer

design.notes: Ribociclib 400 mg starting dose for 3 years plus NSAI; premenopausal women and men also received goserelin. Arm sizes per the final iDFS analysis (PMID 39442617).

clinicalQuestion: Does adding 3 years of ribociclib to a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor improve invasive disease-free survival in a broad stage II-III HR+/HER2- early breast cancer population?

pico.population: Patients with HR+/HER2- early breast cancer, anatomical stage II or III (including N0 with additional risk factors)
pico.intervention: Ribociclib for 3 years plus NSAI (± goserelin)
pico.outcomes: Primary: iDFS. Secondary: distant DFS, RFS, OS, safety

arms.label: Ribociclib + NSAI
arms.regimen: Ribociclib plus letrozole or anastrozole (± goserelin)
arms.dosing: Ribociclib 400 mg/day, 3 weeks on/1 week off, for 3 years; letrozole 2.5 mg/day or anastrozole 1 mg/day for ≥5 years
arms.doseSourceQuote: we randomly assigned patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer in a 1:1 ratio to receive ribociclib (at a dose of 400 mg per day for 3 weeks, followed by 1 week off, for 3 years) plus a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor (NSAI; letrozole at a dose of 2.5 mg per day or anastrozole at a dose of 1 mg per day for ≥5 years) or an NSAI alone.

publications.title: Ribociclib plus Endocrine Therapy in Early Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Prespecified interim iDFS analysis

publications.title: A phase III trial of adjuvant ribociclib plus endocrine therapy versus endocrine therapy alone in patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer: final invasive disease-free survival results from the NATALEE trial.
publications.label: Final iDFS analysis

publications.title: Adjuvant ribociclib plus nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor therapy in patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer: 5-year follow-up of NATALEE efficacy outcomes and updated overall survival.
publications.label: 5-year follow-up with updated OS

outcomes.sourceQuote: At 3 years, invasive disease-free survival was 90.4% with ribociclib plus an NSAI and 87.1% with an NSAI alone (hazard ratio for invasive disease, recurrence, or death, 0.75; 95% confidence interval, 0.62 to 0.91; P = 0.003).

Ribociclib plus NSAI demonstrated significant iDFS benefit over NSAI alone [hazard ratio 0.749, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.628-0.892; P = 0.0012]. The 3-year iDFS rates were 90.7% (95% CI 89.3% to 91.8%) versus 87.6% (95% CI 86.1% to 88.9%).

With a median iDFS follow-up of 55.4 months, ribociclib + NSAI demonstrated persistent iDFS benefit versus NSAI alone [hazard ratio 0.716, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.618-0.829, nominal one-sided log-rank P < 0.0001].
As OS continues to mature, numerical improvement in favor of ribociclib was observed (hazard ratio 0.800, 95% CI 0.637-1.003, nominal one-sided log-rank P = 0.026).

safety.sourceQuote: The 3-year regimen of ribociclib at a 400-mg starting dose plus an NSAI was not associated with any new safety signals.

strengths: Large phase 3 trial including a broader population (stage II-III, selected node-negative) than prior adjuvant CDK4/6 trials
Benefit persisted with extended follow-up after ribociclib completion
limitations: OS immature with no statistically significant difference reported
Primary report was an interim analysis

clinicalImplications.text: Supports adding 3 years of ribociclib to an aromatase inhibitor for stage II-III HR+/HER2- early breast cancer meeting NATALEE eligibility, including selected node-negative patients with additional risk features.

tumourBoardPearl.text: NATALEE extends adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibition to some node-negative stage II disease — check the trial's risk definitions rather than nodal status alone.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMIDs 38507751, 39442617 and 41320342. No total sample size sentence appears in the abstracts; arm sizes taken from PMID 39442617.
